notes: soundLAB 1.4.0: SheetLab is built in. Play › Scan turns a PDF, a scan or a photo of printed sheet music into MIDI and MusicXML, read on your device (nothing is uploaded): then play it on your synth, practise it in the Woodshed, open it as tab, download it or keep it. The first time it asks before downloading the recognition engine (about 107 MB), then it works offline. My library (Play › Library) keeps your scans and the MIDI you play in the Studio, on this device and, with a GitHub key, in the soundLAB repo so every device sees the same library. soundLAB is now open source under the AGPL-3.0 (SheetLab is built on homr). Also in 1.4.0: hands-free practice. A pedal, a button on your synth (a MODX foot switch or Assign switch) or a Bluetooth page-turner pedal now presses Next, Back and Stop, so you never reach for the screen: start a lesson, show the answer, go to the next question or level, retry, end the run, step a Live set. Inside an exercise the keyboard answers too: every multiple-choice answer shows a white key (C, D, E…), play it to answer, and in Woodshed Phrases Next moves to the next phrase. Set it up in Settings › Hands-free control (press Learn, then the button); a LUMI without a pedal can double-tap its lowest key. The bound button only moves practice on — it never plays, sustains or answers. 1.3.1: the Synth tab's buttons work with the MODX. The Arpeggiator, Motion sequencer, Scene and preset buttons now take every tap while the synth sends its MIDI clock (they used to be redrawn under your finger many times a second). The Deck and Live pages connect by themselves: a Connect button the first time, a quiet reconnect after that, and a clear note when the browser blocks MIDI, no synth is plugged in, the LUMI is chosen as the output, or the browser has no MIDI at all (Safari on iPad: use a Web MIDI browser app). On Android, where the app has one MIDI output, picking the synth switches the key lights off instead of playing notes on the synth. soundLAB 1.3.0: the Synth tab. Your synth gets its own tab with three pills: Deck (a play face with faders instead of knobs, a knob-row picker like the MODX, Assign knobs named after what they control, Scenes, chips and an Explain mode that teaches what each control does), Live (Live sets in pages of 16, foot switch and octave-button stepping, Go live with Lock and Panic, whole-setup profiles you can export and import) and Hub (the MIDI Hub, now with key splits and port-aware rules). Presets save a full snapshot: sound, fader values, colour, the app key and scale, a split. One Open on the Play tab opens a MIDI file, a MusicXML score or a text tab and sends it to the synth, the Woodshed or tab view. The Practice tab is now Train, the clef is a header icon like its neighbours, and long page notes moved into tours and tips.
